definition: Privacy Lost is a 2023 short science fiction film directed by Peter Stoel and Robert Berger.
details: It follows a family using augmented reality (AR) and artificial intelligence (AI) devices capable of reading emotional states, raising questions about privacy and manipulation.

explainer.lead: Privacy Lost is a short science fiction film that dramatises what happens when everyday devices can read how people feel. It matters as a cultural touchstone for debates about emotional surveillance and manipulation.

tiers.eli5: Imagine your house gadgets can tell when you're happy or upset, and they use that to nudge what you do. The film shows a family living with exactly that.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers working on affect-sensing or AR products cite the film when discussing consent and data governance. A common pitfall is treating emotional inference as just another sensor reading rather than sensitive personal data.
tiers.paperLevel: Privacy Lost is a 2023 short film directed by Peter Stoel and Robert Berger; it is not a formal method and has no technical definition or stated limits. Its narrative premise is a family using AR and AI devices capable of reading emotional states.

explainer.example: A scene shows a family using AR and AI devices that read their emotional states, illustrating how much personal information such devices expose.
